subject: Proposition 2½ and Municipal Property Taxes
overview: City Councilor Matt Leming delivered an informational presentation explaining how Massachusetts Proposition 2½ caps municipal property tax growth below the rate of inflation, leading to local budgetary challenges. He detailed the mechanics of property assessments, how potential ballot overrides work, and specific cost pressures facing Medford.

items.title: Proposition 2½ Mechanics and Inflationary Impacts
items.summary: Matt Leming explained that Proposition 2½ caps municipal property tax revenue increases at 2.5 percent annually barring new growth, causing city budgets to lose value over time relative to inflation.

items.title: Proposition 2½ Overrides and School Budget Deficit
items.summary: Leming discussed how voter-approved overrides allow municipalities to exceed tax levy limits, noting Medford's projected six million dollar school shortfall and the likelihood of a future override request.

items.title: Property Tax Calculations and Reassessments
items.summary: Leming clarified that the 2.5 percent cap applies to the city's overall tax levy rather than individual tax bills, which can jump sharply when properties are reassessed at higher values.

items.title: Override Cost Estimation and Municipal Budget Pressures
items.summary: Leming provided a formula for estimating household costs under a hypothetical override and reviewed budget pressures affecting city operations, including rising employee health insurance costs and weather-related road deterioration.
